h1: Tube and profile laser cutting machines — Ø0.3″ to 25.2″, 20 to 49 ft tubes, 1.5 to 40 kW
intro: A tube laser cuts round, square, rectangular and open profiles to length and cuts the holes, copes, slots and notches in them in one pass — no saw, no drill, no notcher, no layout — straight from the 3D model, while the loader feeds the next bar. Every tube laser NovoTech sells in Canada is on this page. For tube to Ø14″ on 20 to 40 ft tubes, the tube laser cutters with two or three chucks: the premium Dener E-FTL made in Turkey, accelerating at 1 G, for Ø0.3″ to 13.8″; NovoTech's value-line ULT with two or three chucks for Ø0.4″ to 14.2″; the T series from Ø0.5″ and 1.5 kW; and the high-speed PLUS and ±45° bevel-cutting GPLUS / GT. For structural tube, pipe and beams, the heavy-duty machines: the premium Dener FTL to Ø25.2″ and 12 m bars of 2,600 kg, and the zero-tailing NT and three- and four-chuck ST / HT to Ø25″, 6,600 lb and 49 ft, plus the H-beam profile line. Each family below has its full specification table, photos and brochure, and the buying guide at the foot of the page explains how to choose. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, chiller and tube nesting software, a 1-year warranty and installation, training and parts from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: Standard or heavy-duty tube laser — which should I buy?
faq.a: By the biggest bar you cut. A two- or three-chuck tube laser cutter covers tube to Ø14″ on 20 to 40 ft tubes — railing, furniture, trailer, HVAC, agricultural and most steel-construction work — and is the machine most shops need: the premium E-FTL and the value-line ULT, T and PLUS. A heavy-duty machine with three or four chucks holds beams and pipe to Ø25″, bars of 2,600 – 3,000 kg and 49 ft, and cuts them without tailing — for structural steel, pipe and heavy profiles: the premium FTL and the value-line NT, ST and HT. Both kinds load from a bundle, support the bar as it is cut and take bevel heads.

The premium Dener E-FTL and FTL are built in Turkey with servo-driven chucks (1 G on the E-FTL), a MAX fiber source, a BLT autofocus head and ±0.05 mm repeatability, with parts stocked in Canada — for the shop that runs the tube laser all day. NovoTech's value-line ULT and the Senfeng T / PLUS / GT / NT / ST / HT are built in China with pneumatic chucks, in a wider range of sizes and powers at a lower price; NovoTech stocks the parts and does the service. The premium machine is faster between parts and holds tighter tolerance at high duty.

The E-FTL is the fast machine for the sizes most fabricators use — railings, frames, furniture, trailers, exhaust — Ø0.3″ to 13.8″, accelerating at 1 G and running 394 ft/min on the small chucks. The FTL is built for weight: structural tube and pipe to Ø25.2″ and 12 m bars of 2,600 kg, with ±0.1 mm repeatability on the large chucks. Both take the same 3 – 20 kW sources and bundle loaders.

faq.q: What can a tube laser cut?
faq.a: Round, square, rectangular, oval and open profiles — angle, channel, flat bar — in mild steel, stainless, aluminum, copper and brass, from the chuck's minimum to its maximum size, in wall thicknesses to about 1/2″ (12 kW) or 3/4″ (20 kW). Holes, slots, copes for tube-to-tube joints, tabs and notches for folding, engraving — anything you can draw on the surface of the profile. A 5-axis or 45° bevel head adds weld preparations and mitred corners.

Two chucks (Dener E-FTL / FTL, NovoTech ULT, Senfeng T / PLUS) hold the bar at both ends and cover tube to Ø25″ — the machine most shops need. A third chuck in the middle (NovoTech ULT three-chuck, Senfeng NT) takes over the bar as it shortens, so the last part is cut without a tail. Three and four chucks on the heavy machines (Senfeng ST / HT) carry 49 ft tubes of 6,600 lb without sag for structural sections and towers.

faq.q: What is zero-tailing — the NT series?
faq.a: A two-chuck machine cannot cut the last part of the bar because the rear chuck has to hold something, so a remnant of the chuck length is scrapped from every bar. The NT puts a third chuck in the middle that takes over the bar as it shortens, so the last part is cut and the tail is near zero — on 20 to 40 ft stock to Ø14″ that is several percent of material saved on every bundle.

The number is the largest round tube in millimetres: E-FTL 120 takes Ø0.3 – 4.7″, 180 to 7.1″, 250 to 9.8″ and 350 to 13.8″; FTL 250, 350, 500 and 640 take Ø0.6″ to 9.8, 13.8, 19.7 and 25.2″. Square and rectangular tube is limited by the diagonal, so a 350 chuck takes about 9.8″ square. Buy the chuck for the largest tube you cut regularly — a smaller chuck is faster and holds thin tube better — and the bar length (7, 9 or 12 m) for the stock you buy.

From a bundle: the automatic loader separates one bar, measures it and feeds it to the rear chuck; the front chuck and following supports hold the bar as it is cut; finished parts drop onto the unloading table or conveyor and the remnant is ejected. One operator runs the machine while loading the next bundle. Loading lengths of 20, 30 and 40 ft (6, 9 and 12 m) — or manual loading on the small Senfeng T series.

faq.q: Can it cut bevels and weld preparations?
faq.a: Yes — the 5-axis head on the FTL (optional on the E-FTL) tilts to ±45° so mitred corners, chamfers and weld preparations are cut in the same pass as the holes and copes; the tube arrives at the welding table ready to fit. The seam detector orients welded tube so the seam sits where the drawing puts it.

The CNC imports STEP / IGES solid models of the tube parts, unfolds them onto the profile, nests them along the bar to use the remnant and writes the program — with the cutting database for the material and seam detection to orient welded tube. Offline programming on a PC is standard on both lines.

A 23 ft (7 m) machine needs about 65 ft (20 m) of length including the loader and unloader; a 40 ft (12 m) machine about 100 ft (30 m). 600 V 3-phase with the supplied transformer or 480 V, a chiller (included), assist gas and a dust collector. We lay the machine out for your building before you order.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
